name: Mesurer
tagline: Pixel ruler and guide overlay for React apps and any live page
description: Mesurer is a measurement and alignment overlay by Julien Thibeaut (ibelick). It ships two ways: an MIT-licensed React component you drop into your own app (`<Measurer />`), and a free Chrome extension that works on any site. You get element bounds, draggable horizontal and vertical guides, pixel rulers, Alt-held distance overlays between elements, an x-ray structure mode, a typography inspector, and undo/redo with optional localStorage persistence.
agent_guidance: Reach for the npm package when a human needs to eyeball spacing in a dev build — mount `<Measurer />` beside your app root and gate it behind NODE_ENV, because it renders a global overlay and binds single-letter hotkeys (M, S, G, X, R, H, V) that will collide with any app-level keyboard shortcuts. Prefer the Chrome extension when you are auditing a deployed site or a competitor's page, since it needs no code change and handles Shadow DOM. It measures rendered geometry only; it cannot read your design tokens, so pair it with the actual token source when you are checking a spec, not against it.
why_it_matters: It closes the loop where a design engineer usually screenshots localhost and measures in Figma — the ruler lives in the running app instead. Two delivery modes (library plus extension) from one MIT codebase makes it usable in both dev and audit workflows.
notable_for: React overlay plus Chrome extension from one repo
Alt-held distance overlays between elements
X-ray mode and typography inspector
Undo/redo history for guides

name: Neuform
tagline: Prompt-to-HTML page generator that emits a reusable DESIGN.md
description: Neuform is a hosted AI generator by Meng To (Design+Code) that turns prompts into HTML landing pages, app screens, social concepts, and motion directions, plus a public remix gallery of community templates. Its stated differentiator is that each output carries a DESIGN.md file describing the design system in markdown, so a coding agent can keep building in the same visual language. Pricing is a Free browse tier plus Pro, Max, and Ultra generation plans. Note: every page on the site is client-rendered — the gallery, template list, and price figures could not be read, so no template enumeration or dollar figures are recorded here.
pricing_detail: Free, Pro, Max, and Ultra tiers. Generation starts with a 3-day Pro/Max/Ultra trial that includes 20 prompts; annual billing is advertised at 50% off list while the subscription stays active. Exact dollar figures render client-side and could not be read.
agent_guidance: Treat Neuform as a source of art direction, not a code dependency — the value to you is the DESIGN.md a human hands you, which you can read as a token and style spec before writing components. Do not try to scrape the gallery or the pricing page; both are fully client-rendered and return only a title tag to any non-browser fetch, so ask the user to export or paste the DESIGN.md instead. Its output is standalone HTML, so expect to port rather than reuse if the target repo is a React or Next codebase.
why_it_matters: The DESIGN.md-per-output idea is the interesting part: it turns a one-off generated page into a portable style contract an agent can reuse, which is rarer than another prompt-to-page tool.
notable_for: DESIGN.md emitted with every generation
Public remix gallery of community templates
Built by Meng To of Design+Code

Entirely client-rendered — unreadable to agents

name: Shader Lab
tagline: Browser shader compositor with a WebGPU React runtime for export
description: Shader Lab from basement.studio is a layer-based shader editor in the browser plus a matching npm runtime. You stack effect layers on a timeline, keyframe any parameter or bind it to audio, then take the composition into your own app through @basementstudio/shader-lab. The runtime renders a composition directly in React, feeds it into a Three.js scene as a texture, or runs the effect layers as post-processing over an existing scene. Apache-2.0, WebGPU-only.
agent_guidance: Use this when a marketing hero or background needs a real-time effect that a CSS gradient cannot fake — CRT, dithering, halftone, ASCII, pixel sorting, displacement — and you want the art direction dialled in visually rather than by hand-tuning uniforms. The hard constraint is WebGPU: it will not run in Safari-without-flags or any WebGL-only browser, so always ship a static poster fallback and gate on navigator.gpu. Prefer useShaderLab over the low-level source APIs unless you need manual timing, and remember post-processing must share the same WebGPURenderer as the scene you pass in.
why_it_matters: Most shader tools are either a playground you cannot export from or a library with no authoring UI; this is both halves of the loop from a studio that ships this kind of work commercially. Apache-2.0 on a WebGPU compositor of this quality is unusual.
notable_for: 16 effect layers incl. ASCII, CRT, halftone, pixel sorting, ink
Timeline keyframing and audio-linked parameters
Editor export runs as a React component
Three modes: render, texture, post-processing
Blob tracking with nestable inner effects
Apache-2.0, WebGPU + Three.js TSL

name: AlignUI
tagline: React + Tailwind design system with a code-synced Figma library
description: AlignUI is a commercial design system that ships the same components as React/Tailwind code and as a Figma library kept in sync with it. The free base tier documents roughly 49 components across actions, data display, feedback, forms, layout, navigation, and overlays; the PRO tiers add around 232 blocks in 39 categories, sectoral templates, and the Figma file. Setup runs through a small MIT CLI that scaffolds Tailwind v4.1 with AlignUI tokens. It suits teams that want design/dev parity bought off the shelf rather than assembled.
pricing_detail: Base components free. Figma kit is a one-time purchase: Personal $119 (single user, lifetime updates, commercial use), Startups $349 (5 users, Discord support), Enterprise custom. Lemon Squeezy also lists the code library at ~$299.99-$399.99, the code + Figma bundle at ~$339.99-$599.99, and the AI Template at $149.99. PPP and student discounts are mentioned.
agent_guidance: Reach for AlignUI over shadcn/ui only when the team has already bought the Figma library and wants the code to match it one-to-one — that parity is the whole product, and without it shadcn plus Radix gives you more primitives, a public registry, and an actual MIT licence. The CLI is a Tailwind v4.1 scaffolder, not a component installer, and its README warns it overwrites existing CSS and tailwind.config, so never run it in an initialised repo without backing those up. No accessibility claims are published anywhere on the site, so verify keyboard and ARIA behaviour on Modal, Dropdown, and Command Menu yourself before shipping.
why_it_matters: It is one of the few systems where the Figma file is treated as a build output of the code rather than a drifting parallel artifact, which is exactly the gap most teams lose weeks to.

~232 blocks across 39 categories

name: Dessn
tagline: Design and prototype against your real React repo, in the browser
description: Dessn connects to a GitHub repository, compiles it into a browsable design environment, and lets non-engineers build prototypes as live branches of the production code — no IDE and no localhost. It works with React web apps and imposes no constraint on the CSS or component library in use, and it explicitly never writes or pushes code back to your repo. Teams use it to iterate on real flows instead of static mocks; testimonials cite reusing about 90% of the generated code. Free tier plus per-seat Starter, Teams, and Enterprise plans.
pricing_detail: Free $0/month (one repository compilation, 5 prompts per week); Starter $39/user/month (40 prompts/month); Teams $139/user/month (unlimited prompts, multiple repo support, training opt-out by default, SOC2 + security); Enterprise custom (dedicated support, custom billing, SSO, admin dashboard).
agent_guidance: This is a designer-facing tool, not something you invoke — its explicit pitch is 'no localhost, no MCP', so there is no CLI, no API, and no agent surface for you to drive. Where it touches your work is the output: a designer hands you a Dessn branch built from real repo components, so review it as a normal PR-shaped diff and expect the component imports to already be correct rather than reconstructing from a screenshot. Recommend it only for React web apps, and flag the $39-139 per-seat cost before a team commits.
why_it_matters: It attacks the specific failure where Figma mocks ignore the components that actually exist, by making the repo itself the canvas — and it refuses write access to the repo, which is why design teams get approved to use it.

name: Taste
tagline: Turns saved UI screenshots into a SKILL.md and MCP taste profile
description: Taste is a macOS menu-bar app plus web service that captures UI screenshots you admire (Cmd+Shift+T from Mac, phone, browser, or Figma), runs AI over them to extract colors, spacing, type, radius, and mood, and compiles the result into a living design profile. That profile is published two ways an agent can consume: a SKILL.md written to .cursor/skills/taste/, .claude/skills/taste/, and .agents/skills/taste/, and a live MCP server at mcp.buildwithtaste.com/mcp. It also runs a public Discover feed of community saves and a marketplace where you can rent another designer's profile. Free tier with 5 AI analyses a month; Pro is $20/month.
pricing_detail: Free $0 (15 one-time starter credits, then 5 AI analyses/month, cloud sync, profile generation, SKILL.md export to Cursor/Claude Code/Codex, macOS menu-bar app). Pro $20/month or $150/year, advertised as 37% off (100 AI analyses/month, auto-categorisation and batch import, bring your own OpenAI key for unlimited analyses, Hire directory listing, 6-hour profile regeneration instead of 24h).
agent_guidance: If a user has this installed, the taste profile is already on disk at .claude/skills/taste/SKILL.md — read that file before writing any UI, rather than asking them to describe their aesthetic, and prefer it over the MCP server for a one-shot build since it costs no round trip. Reach for the MCP endpoint only when you need the profile refreshed mid-session after new saves. Treat the output as direction, not spec: it is synthesised from screenshots, so it gives you palette, radius, spacing feel, and mood, but never real component APIs or token names — resolve those from the actual codebase.
why_it_matters: It is the cleanest answer yet to why agent-built UI all looks the same: it makes personal visual taste a durable, portable file instead of a paragraph re-typed into every prompt. Shipping both SKILL.md and MCP rather than picking one is the right call.
